Groups distinguish continuous first-come admission, timed cohorts, first-turn priority and batch random ordering; a call-forward register changes waiting logistics rather than admission priority. Candidate 0 offers the simplest feasible arrangement for two attendants, preserves accessible arrival order and provides inspectable monitoring. Long visits remain its main limitation.

Queue overflow and interruption recovery refine existing mechanisms rather than create new ones. Candidate 5 best combines simple first-come allocation with explicit accessible overflow limits, emergency-access recovery, occupancy responsibility and measurement across both events. Its effects on waiting time remain uncertain.
